thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: S&P 500 On Track For Worst Weekly Decline In 2 Years

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: S&P 500 On Track For Worst Weekly Decline In 2 Years
text:
By Anora M. Gaudiano and Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Dow drops more than 400 points
U.S. stock market indexes fell sharply Friday as investors digested a stronger-than-expected jobs report that stoked inflation fears and contributed to a continued rise in bond yields.
The U.S. economy added 200,000 jobs in January (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-adds-2 -jobs-worker-pay-rises-at-fastest-pace-since-2009-2018-02-02)with the best news coming from the wage growth. Average hourly wages rose 0.3%, pushing the yearly increase to 2.9%, the fastest pace in more than eight years.
Analysts said the market is now pricing in tighter monetary policy if inflation driven by wage growth accelerates.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
The S&P 500 index fell 36 points, or 1.3%, to 2,785 and looked set for a 3% weekly decline. A decline of 3% would the first pullback of this magnitude in 14 months.
Losses on Wall Street were broad-based with 10 of the 11 main sectors trading lower. Energy stocks sold off and traded nearly 4% lower following a drop in oil prices. Technology shares suffered a 2% decline after disappointing earnings and outlook from big tech companies.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell below the psychologically important 26,000 level, trading 400 points, or 1.5%, lower to 25,787. The blue-chip index is set to book 3% weekly decline.
The Nasdaq Composite Index slid 82 points, or 1.1%, to 7,304 and was on track to book a 2.7% weekly loss.
A couple of bruising sessions this week, including Friday's declines have left their mark on the main indexes, with the S&P 500 and Dow looking for the worst weekly performance in more than a year.
What are strategists saying?
"A big wage growth number is the biggest risk to the stock market rally, because it means the Fed may get more aggressive in raising interest rates," said Kristina Hooper, chief global market strategist at Invesco.
"The details of this jobs report, especially the numbers behind the wage growth suggest that companies are competing for workers and the shortage of skilled workers is pushing up wages. The trend in inflation is ticking higher and the big question is whether the incoming Fed, which is more hawkish, will allow the economy run hotter in the short term or tighten aggressively," said Quincy Krosby, chief market strategist, at Prudential Financial.
Other analysts said that higher bond yields will result in the stock market repricing.
The markets are coming to grip with the fact that a 3-3.25% yield factor is not far away. In summary. higher yields will continue to keep pressure on stocks," Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at First Standard Financial, said in a note to clients, referring to the 10-year Treasury rate.
Read:Early-year wage acceleration won't push Fed to hike rates faster or further (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/early-year-wage-acceleration-wont-push-fed-to-hike-rates-faster-or-further-2018-02-02)
Which stocks look like key movers?
Shares in Amazon Inc.(AMZN) climbed 5% after the e-commerce retailer posted fourth-quarter profit and revenue that blew past forecasts.
Read:Amazon heads toward $700 billion valuation thanks to Alexa, AWS and tax gains (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/amazon-heads-toward-700-billion-valuation-thanks-to-alexa-aws-and-tax-gains-2018-02-01)
Apple Inc. shares (AAPL) fell 2.9% after the iPhone maker reported record earnings thanks to sales of the iPhone X, but its forecast fell short of expectations.
See:Live-blog recap of Apple results (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-to-focus-on-iphone-x-sales-live-blog-2018-02-01)
And:Apple earnings show iPhone 'supercycle' isn't happening, and that's OK (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-show-iphone-supercycle-isnt-happening-and-thats-ok-2018-02-01)
Google-parent Alphabet Inc.(GOOGL) slid 4.2%, after missing forecasts for fourth-quarter earnings. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/alphabet-shares-plunge-after-fourth-quarter-earnings-2018-02-01)
Read: Google earnings: Cloud is a $1 billion business, execs say (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/google-earnings-cloud-is-a-1-billion-business-execs-say-2018-02-01)
Mattel Inc.(MAT) surged 9% even after the toy maker posted a steep sales decline during its important holiday period. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mattel-shares-tumble-after-weak-holiday-quarter-2018-02-01)
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mattel-shares-tumble-after-weak-holiday-quarter-2018-02-01)U.S.-listed shares of Deutsche Bank AG(DBK.XE) slid 6.6%, echoing a loss in Frankfurt, after the German bank posted a $2.7 billion loss, owing to the U.S. tax overhaul (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/deutsche-bank-dragged-to-loss-by-us-tax-hit-2018-02-02).
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/deutsche-bank-dragged-to-loss-by-us-tax-hit-2018-02-02) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/deutsche-bank-dragged-to-loss-by-us-tax-hit-2018-02-02)Exxon Mobil Corp.(XOM) earnings fell short of estimates, despite tax benefit. Shares were down 5.1%.
Phillips 66 (PSX) shares fell 1.2% even as the company released earnings above Wall Street's expectations.
J.C. Penney Co.(JCP) shares dropped 1.1% after quarterly earnings release.
What is driving markets?
Stocks were taking a hit as global government bond yields, which have dogged stocks this week, continued to climb on Friday. The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note rose to a four-year high at 2.84%.
Meanwhile, the yield on 10-year German government bunds added 4 basis points to reach 0.76%, close to levels not seen in more than two years. Higher returns on debt securities tend to weaken appetite for stocks and other assets perceived as risky.
Read: U.S. adds 200,000 jobs with wage growth fastest in more than 8 years (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-adds-2 -jobs-worker-pay-rises-at-fastest-pace-since-2009-2018-02-02)
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/january-jobs-bonanza-hiring-likely-rebounded-in-early-2018-2018-02-01)What are other assets doing?
European stocks slumped, driven by a 1.3% slide for the German DAX (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dax-drops-below-13000-after-deutsche-bank-logs-a-hefty-loss-2018-02-02), in part dogged by Deutsche Bank's hefty loss. Asian markets saw a mixed session, with the Nikkei 225 index down 0.9% on disappointing earnings. Gold was flat, while oil futures dropped 1.6%, and the ICE U.S. Dollar Index rose 0.6% to 89.21, thought it is still down 3.1% since the start of the year.
